intro: Most of what I have been asked to fix in month six was a decision nobody made on day one. These are four I now make first, in writing, before the first module exists.

items.title: Tenancy is four decisions, not one
items.rule: Scoped by what. Which tables stay shared. Whether a user can cross tenants. Whether the database enforces it or every query has to remember.
items.cost: A system scoped by branch, when someone asks for company-level reporting, is a rewrite rather than a feature.

items.title: The audit trail is append-only, from the first module
items.rule: Actor, action, resource and detail on every change, and no update or delete path anywhere in the application.
items.cost: Added late, it starts on the day you added it. Every question anyone asks is about the period before.

items.title: A sent document keeps the facts it was sent with
items.rule: Screens read live data. Anything that has left the building carries a snapshot of who it was issued to, frozen at issue time.
items.cost: A vendor moves office, and every purchase order you ever sent now shows an address that was never on it.

items.title: Money is a decimal with a currency, always
items.rule: One type and scale, the currency stored beside every amount even in a single-currency system, and rounding in exactly one place.
items.cost: Rounding in three places with two rules is a reconciliation bug that arrives as a customer complaint.
